subject: Private VPC deployment — control-plane/data-zone segregation & egress hardening
body:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@acmecloud.io>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: netops@acmecloud.io
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial constraints and egress requirements for private VPC deployment

Hi Aditya / Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As promised, attaching our VPC constraints and a quick sketch of preferred routing. High level items:
- Control-plane must not initiate inbound connections to customer-managed control servers; we need to be able to accept connections from the control-plane (pull model) or run a private control-plane in their VPC.
- Data-plane services (inference nodes) will be in isolated subnets with no direct internet egress; all outbound must go through an approved egress gateway/proxy controlled by Acme.
- Audit/log shipping: logs must be pushed to our collector over TLS to 10.40.12.8:6514, with mTLS.
- Firewall rules: minimal open ports; see attached acme_vpc_requirements.xlsx and sketch.

Can you confirm Redwood's recommended topology for the control/data boundary and whether the Redwood control-plane can be deployed in a customer-managed VPC (private control-plane) for this account? If not, what are the recommended fallback patterns (eg: outbound-only control handshake from nodes)?

Elena
NetOps Lead, AcmeCloud

Attachments: acme_vpc_requirements.xlsx, 20270109-routes-and-firewall-sketch.png

----------
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@acmecloud.io>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial constraints and egress requirements for private VPC deployment

Elena — thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. High-level response below, then a proposal for a follow-up deliverable we can share with your security team.

1) Control-plane options
- Private control-plane in customer VPC: supported. We can run the Redwood control-plane components (API, scheduler, config store) inside a customer subnet if they provide a reachable management network and allow the operator account to deploy the control-plane stack (helm/terraform) into a management namespace. This gives maximum control to Acme but requires a small bootstrap window and operator access.
- Hosted control-plane with outbound-only agents: also supported. In that pattern, inference nodes in Acme's VPC make outbound TLS connections to the Redwood control-plane (no inbound). We authenticate with mTLS and keep a persistent upstream connection; telemetry and logs are forwarded over that channel. This avoids us needing any inbound holes.

2) Data-plane segregation and egress
- We'll place inference instances in private subnets without IGW. Egress will be forced through an internal NAT/egress proxy that you manage (as you requested). We will support configuring our container images and sidecar (log/metrics) to use that proxy.
- For audit logs, we can push to your collector over mTLS as long as port 6514 is reachable from the egress gateway.

3) Shortlist of action items for next deliverable
- Redwood to produce a runbook: step-by-step deployment options (private control-plane vs hosted-with-agents), firewall rules, example IAM roles, and a small operator checklist.
- Jonas to draft iptables/filter rules and a sample HAProxy config for the egress gateway.
- Mutual validation meeting next week.

I'll start the runbook draft and upload it to a shared Drive link. Jonas, Mina — can you add network-level details and a quick fallback pattern we can show Acme?

— Aditya
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Elena Martinez <elena@acmecloud.io>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial constraints and egress requirements for private VPC deployment

Adding technical specifics as requested. I've attached a quick sketch (routes-and-firewall-sketch.png) and a short snippet you can paste into your egress proxy.

Notes / assumptions:
- Subnet layout: public/management subnet for control-plane (if hosted in-customer), private for workers. Control-plane components require 6443 (k8s API) internal access and a control-plane port 8443 for our API; both can be bound to internal load balancer only.
- If using hosted control-plane with outbound agents: nodes will egress to control.redwood.example.com:443 over TLS. No inbound rules required. Agents maintain long TCP+TLS multiplexed connections, and we support reconnect/backoff.
- Egress gateway: set up HAProxy with TLS termination + client cert validation for outbound to Redwood. Sample upstream config: 

  # HAProxy sample for outbound to Redwood control-plane
  frontend egress_out
    bind *:3128
    mode tcp
    default_backend redwood_upstream

  backend redwood_upstream
    mode tcp
    option ssl-hello-chk
    server rwd-1 control.redwood.example.com:443 check send-proxy-v2

- IP whitelists: if you want to lock down to Redwood-hosted control-plane, we'll publish a short-lived CIDR set for the deployment window and a small set of FQDNs. For private control-plane this is unnecessary.

Attachment: 20270109-routes-and-firewall-sketch.png

Let me know if you want a 30-min tech deep-dive next Tue.

Jonas
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial constraints and egress requirements for private VPC deployment

Thanks — this is exactly the level we needed. Two quick clarifications before the meeting: 
1) For the private control-plane option, our security team will still require that the control-plane admin endpoints be reachable only from a management network (VPN) and that we have an HSM-backed key for TLS — is that supported by your control-plane helm chart?
2) If we go hosted control-plane + outbound agents, can we enforce forced proxying (everything must go via our egress HAProxy) and have RBAC to prevent agents from dialing arbitrary external addresses?

If both answers are yes, please include the explicit firewall rules and Helm values we should set in your runbook. Also add a short rollback plan in case the agent-based rollout triggers unexpected egress.

Elena

----------
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@acmecloud.io>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 16:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial constraints and egress requirements for private VPC deployment

Elena — quick answers and next steps.

Answers:
- HSM / TLS keys: yes. Our private control-plane Helm chart supports external TLS secrets (you can inject keys from your KMS/HSM into Kubernetes TLS secrets). We'll include a sample values.yaml showing how to reference external certs and the mount points for HSM-backed keys.
- Forced egress & RBAC on agents: yes. Agents can be configured to respect HTTP(S)_PROXY / NO_PROXY environment variables and the agent binary has a restricted network policy mode which prevents arbitrary outbound IPs by only allowing connections to configured endpoints. We'll include the network policy manifests for Calico/iptables.

Deliverables I will upload by EOD today to the shared folder:
- redwood_vpc_runbook_draft.pdf (runbook: deployment options, firewall rules, Helm values, rollback steps)
- sample egress proxy config (HAProxy snippet) — inlined in the runbook and in the Drive folder
- a short checklist for operator handoff and an example permission model for the private control-plane.

Proposed next step: 30-minute joint review on Wed 2027-01-13 at 10:00 PT to walk the runbook and confirm final firewall rules. If that time works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Action items assigned:
- Aditya: upload runbook draft and checklist (EOD today) -> Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyZk-example-link
- Jonas: finalize iptables/Calico manifests and sample HAProxy config -> attached to runbook as separate file
- Mina: owner for post-deploy rollback playbook and QA checklist

Thanks — looking forward to the review.

— Aditya
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
